A labeled fundamental square materially explains which repeated boundary labels denote one edge and how h_(2,0) returns to q_(0,0); representative highlighted star/plaquette supports connect the check formulas with the 18-qubit example. This is an explanatory diagram addition under the expanded editorial criterion, not a proof gap.

The 16 planar vertices and 24 drawn edge segments quotient to 9 vertices and 18 distinct edge qubits; nine face interiors remain distinct.

diagram_math_checks.check: Four blue edges are exactly h_(0,1), h_(1,1), v_(1,0), v_(1,1). Orange boundary of f_(2,2) is h_(2,2), v_(0,2), h_(2,0), v_(2,2). v_(0,2) is drawn on both identified vertical boundaries; h_(2,0) appears orange on top and gold on bottom. These repeated representatives denote the same Pauli factors, not extra support. Translating indices produces all nine stars/plaquettes.

diagram_math_checks.check: The bottom traversal q_(0,0) to q_(1,0) to q_(2,0) to q_(0,0) closes under boundary identification. Mod-two endpoint incidence gives successive e-defect sets {q_(0,0),q_(1,0)}, {q_(0,0),q_(2,0)}, and empty. All plaquette syndromes remain zero because the string is pure Z. No arrows or orientation-dependent sign convention is asserted.
